“Written” realizes ἐν nowhere and the corpus never spends “written” on γράμμα, which it renders “letter”, “letters” and “writings” in all five of its other units while “written” belongs to γράφω. So no part of the single English word answers to either token separately: rule 45, with 2CO.7.10, 2CO.9.6, 2CO.9.7 and 2CO.11.28, and headed on the governed noun. Rule 35 is not the contrast, which needs the preposition spelled into the English word as in “wherewith”. The ASV margin “Greek in letters.” glosses the one word by the whole phrase, against splitting ἐν off as pleonastic under rule 34. Medium because ἐν γράμμασιν is otherwise unattested and the aligned reading stays defensible.

The corpus has no unit folding a repeated antecedent after a relativizer; medium because reading it as a rule 7 helper on the participle stays defensible.
